verdict.rationale: Clerk documents first-party webhooks that send event notifications such as when a user is created or updated. Its CLI can relay webhook deliveries to a local handler and verify signatures, and Billing also emits webhook events. The evidence does not explicitly cover sign-in or session events, and it shows no event-stream alternative, so story coverage is partial. missing for 10: documented sign-in/session event types, an event-stream option, delivery/retry guarantees, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can subscribe to webhooks or event streams for auth events (sign-ups, sign-ins, user changes) to keep my systems in sync

citations.quote: Clerk webhooks allow you to receive event notifications from Clerk, such as when a user is created or updated.
Relay webhook deliveries to your local handler and verify their signatures offline, with no public tunnel service.
